title: Village Chief
text: “That surprised me too. It seems this village has many people of the same race as an acquaintance of mine.”
Elephant chimed in on Father and the others’ conversation there.
“An acquaintance, is it?”
“Yes, someone called Larsazusa.”
“Hoh… Given how you know that girl, and considering your size… race, and bearing, I’d judge you a warrior of Zeltoble, an Elmelo, but what business would you have with this village?”
“! I’m surprised word of me has reached even a place like this.”

Well, Elephant was a famous warrior in Zeltoble, I say. He and Panda apparently fought each other often as rivals in the arena. Panda’s adoptive father supposedly had wide connections through his business dealings. No doubt he’d heard all sorts of things about Zeltoble.
“Elmelo-chan’s a celebrity~ maybe Big Sister should get an autograph.”
“You, of all people… If anything, the moment you showed up, you’d become a celebrity instantly.”
Older Sister was quite the formidable fighter, after all. Even without a Class Up, her skill was first-rate, I say.
“Oh, I’d love to be trampled under that queenly foot~”
“You know something! Where did you hear that from?!”

Elephant glanced at Father and me. Though, he did wince a little at the exchange between himself and Older Sister. Father, too, seemed to be weighing how best to respond. Panda’s adoptive father seemed to relax his guard slightly at Older Sister’s carefree demeanor.
“She’s in my employ, actually. It seems this village happens to be the home village of that same race as the person named Larsazusa.”
“That’s right. Though that girl hasn’t come back to the village.”
“I see. Might the skilled fighter you mentioned be this Larsazusa, perhaps?”
“No, from what you said about it being long ago, that doesn’t sound right.”

Using Panda as a conversational foothold, Father and Panda’s adoptive father continued their back-and-forth. As that exchange dragged on, Panda’s grandfather came stomping over looking thoroughly annoyed. Panda’s adoptive father shot him a look practically screaming don’t come any closer, but he approached anyway, feigning ignorance.
“What’s this? Standing around here giving off such a strange air.”
“There’s no strange air here.”
“Ah, pleasure to meet you. We happened to stop by this village today.”
Both Panda’s adoptive father and Father answered in turn that there was no problem.
“Hah… you’re too on edge. Sure, it’s suspicious enough that humans would bother coming all the way to a village like this, but if they try anything funny, we just beat them back. Simple as that.”

I understood the sentiment, but since the conversation wasn’t progressing, Panda’s grandfather unleashed a positively overwhelming amount of killing intent at Father and me. Hmph… something this mild wasn’t even remotely scary, I say. Father would probably find it terrifying if he took a proportional hit, but so long as we didn’t show any sign of hostility, we ought to be fine.
“Oh my, oh my.”
Elephant and Panda both reacted to the killing intent. But immediately after, it dissipated with a puff.
“So? What business do you have here?”
“They say they came to meet a retired but skilled fighter.”
“Ah, that’s probably me, then. So you’ve met me—now what? Did you come here looking for a match?”
As if to say bring it on, Panda’s grandfather drew out the pipe he carried on his back. Father waved his hands, indicating no, that’s not it.
“No, no. It’s simply that, given how skilled you clearly are, I came to confirm whether you might teach my subordinates a thing or two.”
“Hoh… subordinates, is it.”
“Yes. If your skill is genuine… you could come with us, or you could train them here in the village. As for compensation… I take it money doesn’t interest you much.”
“Well, that’s true.”
“Then… if you refuse, I intend to reach out to another skilled fighter over in Melromarc—someone rumored to fight in a style very similar to yours—and ask them instead.”
“! You know that old hag?! Seriously?!”
At this, Panda’s adoptive father—the peacock beastman—suddenly looked as though something clicked, his expression sharpening.
“Hold on. Could this person… could he be the Shield Hero-sama?”
“Ah? What makes you say that?”
Panda’s grandfather looked puzzled, and his adoptive father explained.

“There’s quiet information circulating in Siltvelt. That the Shield and Spear Heroes have secretly been going back and forth between Melromarc and Siltvelt, protecting the people of the Seaetto territory.”

My word, had rumors even spread this far? I thought, but apparently it was simply that Panda’s adoptive father had an extraordinarily good information network and had picked up on happenings in Siltvelt. Father shifted the shape of his shield to prove he was the genuine article. I followed suit, shifting my spear through various forms as well.
“Shall we have a light spar, then? Seeing my skill firsthand should convince you I’m the real deal, I say.”
“Hoh… very well.”
Panda took a step forward, taking a stance opposite me. So I readied myself as well.
“Motoyasu-kun, even if he’s strong, he’s still an old man, so go easy on him—don’t kill him, okay?”
Oh ho, I was told the exact same thing Father said back when we went to Siltvelt. How nostalgic, I say.
“Naturally, indeed.”
“Let’s see if you’re really the Spear Hero.”
“Come at me anytime, I say.”
“Deryaaaaa!”

The old man Panda swung his pipe down at me. A move I’d seen before. He wove his ki fluidly and slashed upward with it; I deflected it and tried to send the flow of ki back into him to launch him off balance, but—well, I already knew he’d skillfully redirect it.
“Ohh…!”

Even so, when I managed to launch him anyway, Panda’s grandfather’s expression shifted into one of delight. He controlled his fall in midair, landed, slammed his pipe against the ground, and charged. Since we’d sparred so many times, I knew his movements well. A flurry of physical strikes, kicks, then a slam. I deflected all of it and redirected the flowing ki right back at him, slamming him into the ground carefully enough not to injure him.
“Ohoo! My blood’s boiling! Not bad at all!”

Still more to come! Panda’s grandfather grinned as though he’d found a delightful new opponent and unleashed a furious assault on me. I already knew this man fought purely for the joy of it, down to his very core. Relentless, continuous attacks, on and on until he ran out of breath. Ever since reuniting with the old hag, they’d apparently been sparring daily. And once I’d finished deflecting it all, Panda’s grandfather was left panting for breath.
“Hah… hah… well, whatever else, I really have gotten old. Want to keep going, but the body just won’t keep up.”
“Ohh… I see.”
Panda’s adoptive father watched the fight, momentarily rendered speechless.
“Does this convince you now, I say?”
“Yeah… I’ll admit you’ve got skill… but why not just teach them yourself? I’d rather you spar with me instead.”
“There are various reasons for that, you see.”

I wasn’t exactly free enough for that either, I say. I had important work to do, after all, playing with the Filolial-samas. Eventually, I intended to enjoy a nice, pleasant drive with Filo-tan. And have fun with Yuki-chan and Kou too, of course. Sparring now and then was fine, but doing it every single day? No thank you.
“Then, will you hear me out?”
“Yeah. Whether the hero’s real or fake doesn’t matter to me. That technique—only that old hag should know it. If you can get me to meet her, count me in on this deal.”
Panda’s grandfather, apparently, had learned to independently mimic and master ki after his battles with the old hag. He was said to be hoping for a rematch with her.
“Then shall we consider the negotiation settled, I say?”
“Guess so. Can’t help it, huh.”
As if relieved things had worked out well, Panda’s adoptive father raised a hand.
“This really does seem like a wonderful village. A place that you and he protect.”
“That’s right.”
“Larsazusa-san is a lucky one. I’ve never met her, but I can tell.”
“Glad you’d say that. Though lately that girl hardly ever comes back here, and it gets lonely.”
Father gave a light pat on the shoulder of Panda’s adoptive father, who looked downcast at that.
“…Somehow, I get the feeling you’d take a liking to that girl. If you find her, I’d like you to talk to her.”
“Of course. Though I suspect I’d end up causing her all sorts of trouble instead.”
“Hahaha, go easy on her, then.”
In any case, the negotiations seemed to have gone well.
